breaking.headline: Nationwide FAA ground stop traced to a single faulty router
breaking.fact: A routine router swap by contractor L3Harris flooded the FAA's air-traffic network Friday, forcing a nearly five-hour nationwide ground stop — only the second since 9/11. More than 9,200 flights were canceled Friday and 6,200 more Saturday; disruptions stretched into a third day Sunday with 1,900-plus cancellations, though officials expect normal schedules by Monday. No cyberattack is suspected; the FAA has disabled the faulty routers and about 60 similar ones.

breaking.headline: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years
breaking.fact: The Pan American Health Organization has revoked the United States' measles-elimination status, held since 2000, after the same strain circulated uninterrupted for more than a year. The US has logged 5,412 cases in 2026 — the most since 1991 — with cases confirmed in 45 states; PAHO's formal announcement is expected Tuesday.

breaking.headline: Zelenskyy: US floated NATO membership for Ukraine in exchange for Donbas
breaking.fact: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said US negotiators raised for the first time whether Ukraine would withdraw from the Donbas region it still holds in exchange for NATO membership, during US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi. He said Kyiv would not surrender territory but would put a comprehensive package — security guarantees, a strong army, rebuilding funds — to a referendum. Washington has not confirmed the account.

breaking.headline: Lutnick agrees to testify on Nvidia chip exports; Huang summoned for Dec. 3
breaking.fact: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to testify voluntarily before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10 over Nvidia chip exports and the Megaspeed investigation; former Nvidia chief Jensen Huang was asked to appear Dec. 3, under threat of subpoena. The probe centers on whether Nvidia chips reached China through Singapore-based Megaspeed, whose executive is suspected of links to Chinese intelligence.

weekInBrief.headline: IEA sees first oil surplus since the Iran war began
weekInBrief.body: The International Energy Agency said Friday the global oil market will move into surplus in the fourth quarter — the first since the Iran war began in late February — with supply averaging 105 million barrels a day, about 1.7 million above forecast demand. Gulf shipments have recovered faster than demand even as tankers in the region keep coming under attack, and the agency called the market 'showing tentative signs of rebalancing.'

weekInBrief.headline: Bitcoin slides to about $62,100, its lowest since July
weekInBrief.body: Bitcoin fell to about $62,100 in Asian trading Sunday, its lowest since July and roughly 49% below its October record near $126,000, before bouncing back above $65,000. The slide — about 13% on the week, a sixth straight weekly loss — came with roughly $2 billion in leveraged crypto liquidations and continued outflows from US spot bitcoin ETFs, as traders price in another Fed hike. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index printed 10, deep in 'extreme fear.'

weekInBrief.headline: Viking's obesity drug posts strong 13-week data at ObesityWeek
weekInBrief.body: Viking Therapeutics said Sunday that 74% of participants on weekly subcutaneous VK2735 improved by at least one BMI category after 13 weeks, versus 15% on placebo, with improvements across cardiometabolic markers. The dual GLP-1/GIP agonist, presented at ObesityWeek in Washington, is now in Phase 3 trials — another contender in the metabolic race Lilly dominates.

weekInBrief.headline: Finland rejects reported Russian demand to quit NATO
weekInBrief.body: Finland's defence minister called 'absolutely outrageous' a reported Russian proposal — published by Germany's Bild from informal Abu Dhabi talks — that Finland leave NATO and the alliance close its Baltic bases as part of a new European security order. Helsinki says NATO membership is not negotiable; the Kremlin denied making any such demand, though Moscow confirmed it wants NATO forces back to their 1997 positions.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: Iran raised the stakes again this weekend: its Revolutionary Guards claimed a second drone attack on a US radar site at Bahrain's Al-Riffa base on Sunday — Bahrain said it intercepted the drones, as it did after a similar attack Friday — and claimed three tankers struck mines near the strait on Saturday, a claim Reuters could not verify. The US Embassy in Bahrain urged Americans to exercise heightened vigilance, and Washington extended its Jones Act waiver for another 90 days, letting foreign-flagged vessels move oil, fuel, LNG and fertilizer between US ports. On oil, the blockade still holds: Iran has been unable to export any meaningful amount of its own crude for more than two months, while non-Iranian Gulf crude kept moving at about 18.4 million barrels a day in October, roughly 74% of pre-war levels, according to the IEA.

space.headline: ULA's Vulcan fails 10 minutes into flight; 40 Amazon satellites lost
space.body: United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket suffered an anomaly about 10 minutes into flight Sunday and failed to deliver 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites to orbit, on the rocket's return to flight after a February booster anomaly. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman offered NASA's help with the investigation, saying 'Artemis, Moon Base, and the nation need ULA.' The Leo constellation is planned to grow past 3,000 satellites.

space.headline: Blood thinner may slow arthritis joint damage
space.body: Yale researchers screened 980 approved medicines and found dabigatran — a blood thinner normally prescribed to prevent clots and strokes — reduced joint damage and improved movement in mice and macaques with osteoarthritis, by calming the inflammation behind joint breakdown. The study, in Science Translational Medicine, is early work: human trials are still needed, and blood thinners carry serious bleeding risks.

space.headline: Daily pill cuts hereditary swelling attacks by 83%
space.body: A once-daily oral tablet, deucrictibant XR, cut monthly swelling attacks by 83% against placebo in a Phase 3 trial of 85 people with hereditary angioedema, results announced Nov. 12 and presented Nov. 14. Benefit appeared within the first week and held for 24 weeks; maker Pharvaris plans to file for approval in the first half of 2027. The drug is investigational, not yet approved.

space.headline: Gravitational waves could reveal hidden exoplanets, NASA studies show
space.body: Two studies led by NASA astrophysicists show the LISA observatory — three spacecraft set to launch in the mid-2030s to detect gravitational waves — could reveal a new population of exoplanets orbiting double white dwarf stars, with masses and orbital periods mapped in detail. The papers, published Tuesday in The Astrophysical Journal, say the James Webb Space Telescope could then confirm the worlds.

apod.title: A Long Cloud on Mars
apod.credit: ESA, DLR, FU Berlin; Processing: J. Cowart — NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day, November 2, 2026
apod.explanation: A water-ice cloud stretches more than 1,500 km downwind of the volcano Arsia Mons on Mars — the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud, first recorded by NASA's Viking Orbiter 2 in 1977 and imaged here in 2018 by ESA's Mars Express. The cloud forms only in spring and summer mornings, and how it grows in Mars's thin, dust-poor upper air is still an open question.
